Kernel `interval_make_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. An operation that calls this kernel compiles only with the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, and `kairn::traits` exports no constants for it ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

The interval of two values of `T`; the whole line when a bound is a NaN or both are the same infinity, and the empty set when they are reversed:

$$Z = [l_o, h_i].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Interval<T, 1>(lo, hi)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Interval<T, 1>` | implicit for one operand; `constexpr`; does not round |
| `Interval<T, 1>(lo, hi)` | `T`, `T` | `Interval<T, 1>` | each limb converted to `Expansion<T, 1>` first, exactly; `constexpr`; does not round |
| `Interval<T, 1>(a)` | `T` | `Interval<T, 1>` | implicit; $l_o = h_i = a$; `constexpr`; does not round |
| `Interval<T, 1>(a)` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Interval<T, 1>` | implicit; $l_o = h_i = a$; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $h_i$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other, or both are the same infinity ($[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the whole line, $[-\infty, +\infty]$.
- Otherwise, if the bounds are reversed, $l_o > h_i$ ($[+\infty, -\infty]$, and $l_o = +\infty$ or $h_i = -\infty$ with the other finite, among them): $Z$ is the empty set, $(+\infty, -\infty)$.
- Otherwise ($l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$ and $h_i > -\infty$): $Z$ is $[l_o, h_i]$, the same extended real numbers (a zero may change its sign).

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Source

**Algorithm:** constructor of an interval (Milestone 2 listing; equal infinities the whole line, 2026-11-20). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_make_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_make_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# An interval from two values of T supplied by the program, guarded (rule R3); milestone2.md,
# "Interval kernels", "Values of an interval". The whole line when a bound is a NaN, whatever the
# other bound is, and when both bounds are the same infinity, [+inf, +inf] or [-inf, -inf]: a value
# from the program that is not finite never makes the empty set (decided on 2026-11-20 for a NaN, a
# NaN saying that something failed upstream, and on the same day for an infinite point, which IEEE
# 1788 makes the empty set). Otherwise the empty set when lo > hi (rv, false with a NaN), [+inf, -inf]
# and lo = +inf with a finite hi among them; otherwise [lo, hi], [-inf, +inf], [lo, +inf] and
# [-inf, hi] included. For every precision.
# The IEEE-model proof (proofs/theories/IeeeInterval1.v) is of the rule before, that the two pairs
# of the same infinity give the empty set, and is being redone for this one: unverified until then.

gl = guard(lo)
gu = guard(hi)
ok = le(gl, gu)
nl = lt(gl, const inf)
mi = neg(const inf)
nu = lt(mi, gu)
va = and(ok, nl)
v  = and(va, nu)
rv = lt(gu, gl)
el = select(rv, const inf, mi)
eu = select(rv, mi, const inf)
zl = select(v, gl, el)
zu = select(v, gu, eu)
```
